segments.text: Welcome to Harbor Lines. Today I'm talking with Dana Okafor, chief engineer of the Port Alder ferry authority.
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: Thanks for having me. It has been a long few years on the water.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Let's start with the decision people still argue about. What happened in 2019?
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: In 2019 the board voted to postpone dredging the channel to save about four million dollars.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: I was the one who recommended the deferral, and I regret it.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: What did that do to the channel?
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: At low tide the channel depth fell from eleven meters to 9.1 meters.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: And what were the consequences for the ferries?
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: We had fourteen groundings in 2023.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Repairs and refunds from those groundings cost about 6.2 million dollars in 2023.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Meanwhile you ordered new boats.
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: In 2022 we ordered two battery-electric ferries from a yard in Gdansk, at thirty-eight million dollars each.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Why go electric?
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: Diesel fuel costs us about 2.9 million dollars a year, and we expect the electric ferries to cut that by seventy percent.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Can the docks handle the charging?
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: Not yet. We need a 22 megawatt shore-power upgrade, which costs twenty-seven million dollars.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Northline Power is paying forty percent of that.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Any surprises with the batteries?
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: Battery capacity drops eighteen percent below minus five Celsius.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: To compensate we added a third charging stop at Fenwick Point.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Tell me about the passengers.
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: We carry about 1.8 million riders a year.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Ridership fell seven percent last year, and most of that was caused by delays.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: I hear the fishermen were worried about the construction.
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: We reached a compromise with the fishermen's co-op. Pile driving only happens from October to March.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: That is outside the April to September herring season, and in return the co-op gives us staging access to its pier.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: What would you tell other ferry operators?
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: Price deferred maintenance honestly. Do not treat it as free money.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: And test batteries in the worst season first, not the easiest one.
segments.speaker: Speaker B

segments.text: Dana Okafor, thank you for your time.
segments.speaker: Speaker A

segments.text: My pleasure.
segments.speaker: Speaker B
